question: Find the part with an error: I am looking forward to meet (A) / you at the conference, as (B) / we have much to discuss. (C)
explanation: 'Look forward to' takes a gerund: 'to meeting'.

question: Improve the part in capitals: She prefers walking in the morning RATHER THAN to cycle in the evening.
explanation: 'Prefer X to Y' with gerunds.

question: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct? (Set 6)
options: Hardly had she entered when the lights went out.
Hardly she had entered when the lights went out.
Hardly had she entered than the lights went out.
Hardly did she entered when the lights went out.
explanation: 'Hardly had ... when' is the correct pattern.

question:
Rearrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
P. Some banks have therefore started special help desks for senior customers.
Q. Yet millions of older citizens struggle with online banking.
R. Digital literacy is now as essential as basic reading and writing.
S. These desks teach them how to use apps safely.
explanation: Statement, problem, response, detail.

question: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct? (Set 5)
options: He suggested me to apply for the post.
He suggested me that apply for the post.
He suggested to me applying for post.
He suggested that I apply for the post.
explanation: 'Suggest' takes a that-clause with the subjunctive.

question: Improve the part in capitals: The new scheme is more beneficial THAN ANY scheme launched so far.
explanation: Comparison within the same class needs 'other'.

question: Choose the word opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: The trust received a MUNIFICENT donation from an alumnus.
explanation: Munificent means very generous; stingy is the opposite.

question: The committee (A) / have decided to (B) / postpone it's meeting. (C)
explanation: 'its' (possessive) is correct; 'it's' means 'it is'.

question: Find the part with an error: The proposal was not only (A) / cost-effective but also (B) / it was easy to implement. (C)
explanation: Faulty parallelism: 'not only cost-effective but also easy to implement'.

question: Improve the part in capitals: The manager insisted that every employee SUBMITS the report by Friday.
explanation: Subjunctive after 'insisted that' takes the base form.

question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: To throw cold water on a plan.
explanation: It means to dampen enthusiasm.

question: Choose the word closest in meaning to the word in capitals: The union leader's INTRANSIGENT stance stalled the talks.
explanation: Intransigent means refusing to change one's position.

question:
Rearrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
P. A downgrade, in contrast, makes borrowing costlier.
Q. Credit rating agencies assess the ability of borrowers to repay their debts.
R. That is why governments and companies guard their ratings closely.
S. A high rating lets a borrower raise funds at a lower interest rate.
explanation: Definition, benefit, contrast, conclusion.

question: Improve the part in capitals: I wish I WAS taller.
explanation: Subjunctive after 'wish'.

question: Improve the part in capitals: She is THE TALLER of the three sisters.
explanation: Superlative for more than two.

question: Improve the part in capitals: The director along with his friends WERE invited to the function.
explanation: The subject is the singular 'director'.

question: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct? (Set 9)
options: No sooner had he arrived than the meeting began.
No sooner did he arrive than the meeting began.
No sooner had he arrived when the meeting began.
No sooner he arrived than the meeting began.
explanation: 'No sooner had ... than' is the standard form.

question: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct? (Set 8)
options: The reason why he resigned is because of ill health.
He resigned because he was ill.
Reason for him to resign was due because ill health.
The reason he resigned is due because ill health.
explanation: Only option B avoids redundancy and faulty constructions.

question: Find the part with an error: Whom do you think (A) / will be appointed as (B) / the next branch head? (C)
explanation: 'Who' is the subject of 'will be appointed'.

question: Improve the part in capitals: She is quite capable TO HANDLE the pressure of the job.
explanation: 'Capable' is followed by 'of' plus a gerund.

question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: To be at loggerheads.
explanation: It means quarrelling or disagreeing sharply.

question:
Rearrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
P. The usual tool is the policy interest rate.
Q. Inflation erodes the purchasing power of money over time.
R. Raising it makes borrowing costlier and thus cools demand.
S. Central banks therefore try to keep it within a target band.
explanation: Problem, response, tool, mechanism.

question: Improve the part in capitals: Having finished the audit, THE REPORT WAS SENT BY THE MANAGER to the head office.
options: the report being sent by the manager
the report had been sent by the manager
explanation: The participial phrase must modify the manager.

question: The speaker's _____ delivery failed to _____ the restless audience.
explanation: A monotonous delivery cannot captivate an audience.

question: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct? (Set 2)
options: I have been working here since five years.
She doesn't hardly speak to anyone.
The committee has completed its inquiry.
Between you and I, the plan will fail.
explanation: The collective noun acts as a unit, matching 'its'.

question: Choose the word closest in meaning to the word in capitals: The clerk's REMISS attitude led to the loss of records.
explanation: Remiss means careless of duty.

question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: To have a chip on one's shoulder.
explanation: It means holding a lingering resentment.

question: The prosecution's case was so strong, thanks to a _____ of evidence, that the court was compelled to _____ bail.
explanation: Abundant evidence leads to denial of bail.

question: Improve the part in capitals: I look forward TO MEET you at the conference.
explanation: 'To' here is a preposition followed by a gerund.

question: Find the part with an error: The report, which was (A) / drafted by two juniors and I, (B) / was well received by the board. (C)
explanation: Object of the preposition 'by' needs 'me', not 'I'.
